title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 310: Giants and Dwarfs: Rethinking the Island Rule
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 310 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

Giants and Dwarfs: Rethinking the Island Rule

Paragraph 1. In 1964, scientist J. Bristol Foster noticed something strange about animals living on islands. Small animals from mainlands, such as mice and rats, often grew much bigger on islands. At the same time, huge animals like elephants and hippos grew much smaller. People found ancient bones of pony-sized mammoths and giant rats as big as dogs! For a long time, scientists called this 'Foster's Rule' and thought it worked everywhere.

Paragraph 2. Today, scientist Dr. Claire Moreau thinks that old rule is too simple. She explains that animal size on islands changes for two practical reasons: safety and food. On mainlands, small mice must stay tiny so they can hide inside small burrows (holes in the ground) from hungry birds and foxes. On remote islands without hunting animals, small mice do not need to hide, so growing bigger helps them win food.

Paragraph 3. Big plant-eating animals have the opposite story. On continents, large animals need huge bodies to protect themselves from wolves and big cats. However, those big hunters rarely reach distant islands because islands do not have enough food for them. Without dangerous hunters and with less grass to eat on a small island, big plant-eaters slowly become smaller over many years.

Paragraph 4. Still, Dr. Moreau checked over two thousand island animal groups and found a surprise. Foster's Rule does not work for every kind of animal: bats and meat-eating animals show no clear size change. Also, local climate and mountain shape often matter more than island size. Nature never follows one simple rule for every creature.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...huge animals like elephants and hippos grew much smaller."
Đoạn 2: "...hide inside small burrows (holes in the ground)..."
Đoạn 3: "...protect themselves from wolves and big cats."
Đoạn 4: "Also, local climate and mountain shape often matter more..."

q5.text: What did scientist J. Bristol Foster discover about giant rats and mammoths on islands?
options: A. Rats stayed tiny while mammoths grew twice as tall.
B. Both rats and mammoths disappeared because of cold weather.
C. Small rodents grew huge while large mammoths became pony-sized.
D. Neither rats nor mammoths ever lived on remote islands.

steps: Đoạn 1: Chuột phát triển to như chó, còn voi ma-mút thu nhỏ bằng ngựa con.

q6.text: Why do mice grow bigger on islands without predators?
options: A. Larger bodies help them get more food safely.
B. They learn how to swim across deep oceans.
C. Island trees force them to climb higher branches.
D. People feed them extra crops every winter.

steps: Đoạn 2: Không cần trốn kẻ săn mồi nên cơ thể to hơn giúp chúng giành thức ăn tốt hơn.

q7.text: Why do big plant-eating animals become smaller on islands?
options: A. They sleep longer during warm island summers.
B. Wolves hunt only the tallest plant-eaters on islands.
C. Island caves are too narrow for big animals.
D. They face no big predators and have less food to eat.

steps: Đoạn 3: Không có thú dữ đe dọa và thiếu thức ăn trên đảo nhỏ.

q8.text: What did Dr. Claire Moreau show in the last paragraph?
options: A. Bats always grow into giants on every island.
B. Foster's Rule does not apply to all animal groups.
C. Island size is the only factor changing body weight.
D. Scientists should stop digging up ancient fossils.

steps: Đoạn 4: Quy luật Foster không đúng với mọi loài (như dơi và thú ăn thịt).
